live_capture_notes: attempt 1 was an environment contention: a session the first probe leaked held the chrome-direct lifecycle lock; closing my own sessions cleared it
attempt 2 read a real post and sealed it (body sha256 verified against the reported content_hash) but the run was reported FAIL because one post did not repeat a hard-coded phrase pair
attempt 3 showed the adapter aborting the whole page on the first collapsed article, which is what a 20-item window hits on real lazy-rendered X results
attempt 4 exposed the domain contract: captureSourcePageBound returned before sealing whenever Page.Failure was set, so a prefix and its evidence count could never agree

attempt 5 is the corrected behaviour: 2 real posts sealed, evidence/items equal, page_complete false, cursor observed_tail:2106688975465586698 persisted as pending with covered_until null and revision 2, claim verdict NOT_CORROBORATED recorded separately

not_verified_by_design: the card's 健康/覆盖与UI一致 half is NOT exercised here. The product already models this: internal/domain/research.go:164 builds per-source coverage entries with status PARTIAL and gap_reason, research.go:183 restates PARTIAL when the source query changed, research_acceptance.go:262 sets the cycle outcome to PARTIAL, and apps/web/src/screens.jsx renders cycle.source_coverage (source id, status tag, gap_reason or record_count, requested window) in the 来源覆盖 sections of the workbench and cycle screens. What W07-02 actually ran is the capture layer: real sources, real cursors, real sealed bytes. No research cycle was advanced over these captures, so no row here grades cycle.source_coverage against the cursor state, and nothing grades the rendered UI against that field. Both are owed, and the honest place for them is a cycle-level case rather than a paraphrase in this card.
